column1: Game Start & Initial State
column26: Covers the initial state of the Bird Game and the functionality required to begin gameplay, including the initial display, idle state and supported controls for starting the game.

column1: Bird Controls & Movement
column26: Covers player control of the bird using keyboard, mouse and on-screen controls, including upward and downward movement, jumping and gravity behaviour.

column1: Obstacle Behaviour
column26: Covers obstacle movement, obstacle recycling, randomisation of the opening position and the size and positioning of the obstacle opening.

column1: Scoring
column26: Covers the Bird Game scoring behaviour, including the starting score, awarding points when an obstacle is successfully passed, preventing duplicate scoring and displaying the current score.

column1: Collision & Game Over
column26: Covers collision detection with obstacles and game boundaries, safe passage through the obstacle opening, and the behaviour of the game after Game Over

column1: Restart
column26: Covers restarting the Bird Game after Game Over, including resetting the score, bird position, obstacle state, start instructions and returning the game to its initial idle state.

column1: Compatibility & Responsiveness
column26: Covers browser compatibility and usability across supported screen sizes, including Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox and availability of the on-screen controls on smaller screens

column1: Display the initial game state
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want to see the initial game state when I open the game so that I know the game is ready to be played.

*Requirement Reference*

BR-FR-001

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The bird is visible when the game first opens.
# The first obstacle is visible when the game first opens.
# The score displays 0 when the game first opens.
# Short instructions explaining how to start the game are visible when the game first opens.

column1: Keep the game idle until the player starts
column26:
*User Story*
As a player, I want the game to remain idle until I choose to start so that gameplay does not begin before I am ready.

*Requirement Reference*
{{BR-FR-002}}

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The game remains idle when it first opens.
# The bird does not begin gameplay movement before a supported control is used.
# The obstacle does not begin moving before a supported control is used.
# Gameplay begins only after the player uses a supported control.

column1: Start the game using supported controls
column26:
*User Story:*
As a player, I want to start the game using any supported control so that I can begin gameplay using my preferred input method.

*Requirement Reference:*
{{BR-FR-003}}

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# Pressing the Up Arrow can start the game.
# Pressing the Down Arrow can start the game.
# Pressing Space can start the game.
# Clicking inside the game area can start the game.
# Pressing either on-screen control button can start the game.
# Once a supported control is used, gameplay begins.

column1: Control the bird using directional controls
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want to move the bird upward and downward using keyboard or on-screen controls so that I can control its position during gameplay.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-004
BR-FR-005
BR-FR-008

*Acceptance Criteria*

# While the Up Arrow key is held during gameplay, the bird moves upward.
# Releasing the Up Arrow stops the manual upward movement.
# While the Down Arrow key is held during gameplay, the bird moves downward.
# Releasing the Down Arrow stops the manual downward movement.
# Holding the on-screen Up button produces the same continuous upward movement as holding the Up Arrow key.
# Holding the on-screen Down button produces the same continuous downward movement as holding the Down Arrow key.
# Releasing either on-screen control button stops the corresponding manual movement.

column1: Make the bird jump using Space or mouse click
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want to make the bird jump using the Space key or a mouse click so that I can quickly move the bird upward during gameplay.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-006
BR-FR-007

*Acceptance Criteria*

# Pressing Space during gameplay gives the bird one upward jump.
# A single press of Space produces one jump.
# Clicking inside the game area during gameplay gives the bird one upward jump.
# A single mouse click produces one jump.
# Both Space and mouse click produce the same intended upward-jump behaviour.

column1: Apply gravity when the bird is not manually controlled
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want gravity to pull the bird downward when I am not manually controlling it so that the game behaves consistently and requires continuous player interaction.

*Requirement Reference*

BR-FR-009

*Acceptance Criteria*

# Gravity becomes active after gameplay has started.
# When the player is not manually moving the bird, gravity gradually moves the bird downward.
# Gravity does not move the bird before gameplay has started.
# Manual movement controls can temporarily change the bird's movement while gameplay is active.
# When manual movement stops, gravity continues to pull the bird downward.

column1: Move and recycle the obstacle
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the obstacle to move continuously across the game area and return for another pass so that gameplay can continue without requiring new obstacles to be created.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-010
BR-FR-011

*Acceptance Criteria*

# During gameplay, the obstacle moves from the right side of the game area towards the left.
# The obstacle moves at a constant speed during each pass.
# When the obstacle completely leaves the left side of the game area, it is reset to the right side.
# After being reset to the right side, the obstacle begins another pass across the game area.
# The obstacle recycling behaviour continues while gameplay remains active.

column1: Randomise and constrain the obstacle opening
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the obstacle opening to change position while remaining a consistent and valid size so that each obstacle pass provides variation without creating an impossible route.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-012
BR-FR-013

*Acceptance Criteria*

# Each time the obstacle is reset, the vertical position of the opening is randomised.
# The obstacle opening remains 160 pixels high.
# The opening remains fully inside the playable area.
# The opening does not extend beyond the top boundary of the playable area.
# The opening does not extend beyond the bottom boundary of the playable area.
# The opening is positioned so that obstacle area remains visible both above and below the opening

column1: Initialise and display the player's score
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want my score to start at zero and remain visible during gameplay so that I can clearly track my progress.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-014
BR-FR-017

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The player's score is set to 0 when a new game is opened.
# The score displays 0 before the player earns any points.
# The current score remains visible while gameplay is running.
# The displayed score reflects the player's current score throughout gameplay.

column1: Award one point for each successful obstacle pass
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want my score to increase when I successfully pass an obstacle so that my progress is accurately recorded.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-015
BR-FR-016

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The score increases by 1 when the whole obstacle has moved past the bird horizontally without a collision.
# The score does not increase before the obstacle has been completely passed.
# A successful pass increases the score only once.
# The same obstacle pass cannot add more than one point.
# After the obstacle is reset and successfully passed again, the score can increase by another 1 point.
# If the bird collides with the obstacle before successfully passing it, no point is awarded for that pass.

column1: Detect collisions and safe obstacle passage
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the game to correctly distinguish between collisions and safe passage through an obstacle so that Game Over occurs only when I hit an obstacle or game boundary.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-018
BR-FR-019
BR-FR-020

*Acceptance Criteria*

# Collision with the upper pipe ends the game.
# Collision with the lower pipe ends the game.
# Reaching the top boundary of the playable area ends the game.
# Reaching the bottom boundary of the playable area ends the game.
# Passing through the clear obstacle opening does not end the game when the bird remains inside the opening.
# Game Over is triggered only when one of the defined collision conditions occurs.

column1: Handle the Game Over state
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the game to clearly enter a Game Over state after a collision so that I know gameplay has ended and can see my final result.

*Requirement Reference*

BR-FR-021

*Acceptance Criteria*

# When a Game Over condition occurs, gameplay stops.
# The obstacle stops progressing as active gameplay.
# No further points are added after Game Over.
# The player's final score is displayed.
# Movement controls no longer move the bird after Game Over.
# The Game Over state remains active until the player chooses an available restart action.

column1: Provide a Restart action after Game Over
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want a Restart option after Game Over so that I can start another game without reloading the application.

*Requirement Reference*

BR-FR-022

*Acceptance Criteria*

# A Restart button is available after Game Over.
# The Restart button is visible on the Game Over screen.
# The Restart button can be selected by the player after Game Over.
# The Restart option is not required as part of normal active gameplay.

column1: Reset the game to its initial idle state
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the game to reset properly when I select Restart so that I can begin a new game from the same clean starting state.

*Requirement References*

BR-FR-023
BR-FR-024

*Acceptance Criteria*

# Selecting Restart resets the player's score to 0.
# The bird returns to its starting position.
# The obstacle returns to its initial state.
# The start instructions are displayed again.
# After Restart, the game returns to the initial idle state.
# Gameplay does not begin automatically after Restart.
# The game waits until the player uses a supported control before gameplay begins again.

column1: Support the required desktop browsers
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the Bird Game to work consistently in the supported desktop browsers so that I can play the game using a commonly supported browser.

*Requirement Reference*

BR-NFR-001

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The game is usable in the current supported version of Google Chrome.
# The game is usable in the current supported version of Microsoft Edge.
# The game is usable in the current supported version of Mozilla Firefox.
# Core gameplay functionality behaves consistently across the three supported browsers.
# No browser-specific issue prevents the player from completing the core gameplay flow in any supported browser.

column1: Maintain usability on smaller screens
column26:
*User Story*

As a player, I want the game to remain usable on smaller screens so that I can still view and control the game when less screen space is available.

*Requirement Reference*

BR-NFR-002

*Acceptance Criteria*

# The game layout remains usable when displayed on a smaller supported screen.
# Essential game elements remain visible and accessible.
# The on-screen Up control remains available on smaller screens.
# The on-screen Down control remains available on smaller screens.
# The player can use the on-screen controls without essential game content becoming inaccessible.
# The layout does not prevent the player from completing the core gameplay flow on a supported smaller screen.

column1: First obstacle is not visible in the initial game state
column26:
*Defect Description*

The first obstacle is not visible when Bird Game v1 initially loads. The initial state therefore does not fully meet BR-FR-001.

*Preconditions*

* Bird Game v1 local build is available.
* Google Chrome is open.
* No game control has been used.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Open {{source/index.html}} in Google Chrome.
# Allow the game to load.
# Do not press any keyboard key, click the game area, or use the on-screen controls.
# Observe the initial game state.
# Reload the page using {{Ctrl + R}}.
# Again, observe the initial game state without providing any input.

*Expected Result*

The initial game state should display:

* the bird;
* the first obstacle;
* score = 0;
* start instructions.

*Actual Result*

The bird is visible, score is displayed as 0, and the start instruction is displayed. However, the first obstacle is not visible in the initial game state.

*Reproducibility*

Reproduced after page reload using {{Ctrl + R}}.

*Environment*

Windows desktop
Google Chrome 151.0.7922.109 (64-bit)
Bird Game v1 local build
{{source/index.html}}

*Traceability*

* Requirement: BR-FR-001
* Jira Story: BG-8
* Test Case: TC-START-001
* Execution Task: BG-26

column94:
10/Aug/26 7:21 PM;712020:31d0c1d1-693d-4aed-b192-4562fff4a957;*Fix implemented and retested successfully.*

*Root Cause*
The obstacle was initially positioned at the full width of the game container ({{game.clientWidth}}). Because the obstacle itself has a width, this placed the entire obstacle outside the visible game area on initial load.

*Fix Applied*
The initial obstacle position was changed so that its own width is deducted from the game width:

{{let obstacleLeft = game.clientWidth - obstacle.offsetWidth;}}

This places the first obstacle fully inside the visible game area while preserving the existing obstacle movement and recycling behaviour.

*Retest Results*

* TC-START-001 — PASS
Bird visible, first obstacle visible, score displayed as 0, and start instructions visible.
* TC-START-002 — PASS
Bird remained stationary before player input and the obstacle also remained stationary before player input.

*Retest Evidence*

* {{TC-START-001_BG-27_RETEST_PASS_2026-08-10.png}}
* {{TC-START-002_BG-27_RETEST_PASS_2026-08-10.png}}

The defect is no longer reproducible on the corrected build. BG-27 is ready for closure.

column1: Mouse click does not start gameplay from the initial state
column26:
*Defect Description*

Clicking inside the Bird Game area does not start gameplay from the initial state, even though mouse click is defined as a supported start control.

*Preconditions*

* Bird Game v1 local build is available.
* The game is loaded in Google Chrome.
* The game is in its initial idle state.
* No keyboard or on-screen control has been used.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Open {{source/index.html}} in Google Chrome.
# Allow the game to load.
# Do not press any keyboard key or use the on-screen controls.
# Click once inside the game area.
# Observe the game behaviour.
# Reload the page using {{Ctrl + R}}.
# Repeat the mouse click inside the game area.

*Expected Result*

A single mouse click inside the game area should:

* start gameplay;
* make the bird perform one upward jump;
* remove the start instruction.

*Actual Result*

Clicking inside the game area did not start gameplay. The bird did not perform an upward jump and the start instruction remained visible.

*Reproducibility*

The issue was reproduced after reloading the page and repeating the mouse-click action.

*Environment*

Windows desktop
Google Chrome 151.0.7922.109 (64-bit)
Bird Game v1 local build
{{source/index.html}}

*Traceability*

* Requirement: BR-FR-003
* Jira Story: BG-10
* Test Case: TC-START-006
* Execution Task: BG-26

*Evidence*

{{TC-START-006_Mouse_Click_Start_FAIL_2026-08-10.png}}
column94:
10/Aug/26 8:53 PM;712020:31d0c1d1-693d-4aed-b192-4562fff4a957;*Controlled retest completed; defect not reproducible in controlled Chromium execution.*

The current source was reviewed and BG-28 was retested using the build containing the BG-27 obstacle-position correction. No BG-28-specific code change was made.

*Controlled Retest Result*

* 20 consecutive mouse-click start attempts executed in Chromium.
* 20/20 attempts passed.
* Each successful attempt started gameplay, caused the bird to move upward, removed the start instruction and started obstacle movement.
* No JavaScript page errors were observed during the controlled run.

*Source Review*
The game container has a click event listener that invokes {{jump()}}. The {{jump()}} function invokes {{startGame()}} when gameplay has not already started.

*Local Manual Observation*
Manual testing in the Windows Chrome/local-file environment produced inconsistent behaviour: one retest passed and a later retest failed. Therefore, the original defect cannot yet be classified as definitively resolved.

*Current Assessment*
BG-28 is not reproducible under controlled Chromium retesting. No additional code change is justified at this stage without a consistently reproducible failure condition.

Status should remain open pending review of the environment-specific/manual inconsistency.
column95:
10/Aug/26 8:53 PM;712020:31d0c1d1-693d-4aed-b192-4562fff4a957;*Final disposition: Not Reproducible*

The original mouse-click failure was recorded during manual testing. Subsequent investigation produced inconsistent manual behaviour, while controlled Chromium retesting completed 20/20 successful executions.

No BG-28-specific code change was made, and no consistently reproducible failure condition could be identified.

The defect is therefore being closed as *Not Reproducible*, rather than Fixed.

Original failure evidence and controlled retest evidence remain attached for traceability.
